issues.legal_issue: A judgment of a single judge in a petition invoking writ jurisdiction is appealable to a division bench when the High Court’s charter provides an intra-court appeal and no applicable exclusion bars it.
material_facts: The court considered whether a single judge’s judgment in a petition invoking writ jurisdiction could be appealed to a division bench under the High Court’s charter.

The charter provided for an appeal from a single judge’s judgment, subject to specified exclusions, and the court found that a proceeding under Article 226 was not excluded merely because of the jurisdiction exercised.
issues.conclusion: An intra-court appeal lies from a single judge’s judgment in a proceeding under Article 226, provided the charter’s conditions are met and the appeal is not otherwise barred.
issues.legal_principle: The charter’s appeal provision covers judgments given in any jurisdiction unless that jurisdiction or judgment is expressly excluded. Article 225 preserves the existing High Courts’ powers and the continued operation of their charters and rules; the references in the charter to Section 108 of the Government of India Act, 1915, are read as references to the corresponding provision in Article 225. A proceeding under Article 226 is an original proceeding and, when it concerns civil rights, an original civil proceeding. The court relied on National Sewing Thread Co. Ltd. v. James Chadwick & Bros. Ltd., South Asia Industries Private Ltd. v. S.B. Sarup Singh, State of Uttar Pradesh v. Dr. Vijay Anand Maharaj, Commissioner of Income-tax v. Ishwarlal Bhagwandas, Ramesh v. Seth Gendalal Motilal Patni, Arbind Kumar Singh v. Nand Kishore Prasad, and Ahmedabad Mfg. & Calico Ptg. Co. Ltd. v. Ram Tahel Ramnand.

rule.if: writ_jurisdiction_proceeding and single_judge_judgment and charter_allows_intra_court_appeal and appeal_not_otherwise_barred

predicates.writ_jurisdiction_proceeding: The proceeding asks the High Court to issue a direction, order, or writ to a person, authority, or government.
predicates.single_judge_judgment: A single judge of the High Court decides the proceeding.
predicates.charter_allows_intra_court_appeal: The High Court’s charter provides an appeal from a single judge’s judgment in the relevant category of proceeding.
predicates.appeal_not_otherwise_barred: No applicable exclusion or other enactment bars an appeal from the judgment.

issues.definition: When a single judge decides a proceeding seeking writ relief, an intra-court appeal lies if the charter provides for it and no applicable bar prevents it.

issues.legal_issue: A division-bench appeal does not lie from a single judge’s judgment exercising supervisory jurisdiction over subordinate courts or tribunals when the High Court’s charter excludes such judgments from appeal.
material_facts: The widow’s petition before the single judge was under Article 227 and challenged the Revenue Tribunal’s order.
The single judge set aside the Tribunal’s order and restored the Sub-Divisional Officer’s order.
The appellants’ intra-court appeal was dismissed as not maintainable, and they challenged that dismissal.
issues.conclusion: No intra-court appeal lies from a single judge’s judgment given in a proceeding under Article 227; the appeal in this case was rightly dismissed as not maintainable.
issues.legal_principle: Article 227 confers supervisory jurisdiction, distinct from the power to issue writs under Article 226, and a proceeding under Article 227 is not an original proceeding. The charter’s exclusion of orders made in the exercise of the power of superintendence is read to cover orders made under Article 227. The court relied on Section 8 of the General Clauses Act, 1897, Section 38 of the Interpretation Act, 1889, National Sewing Thread Co. Ltd. v. James Chadwick & Bros. Ltd., Ahmedabad Mfg. & Calico Ptg. Co. Ltd. v. Ram Tahel Ramnand, Waryam Singh v. Amarnath, and State of Gujarat v. Vakhatsinghji Vajesinghji Veghela.

rule.if: supervisory_review_proceeding and single_judge_disposition and order_exercises_supervisory_power and charter_excludes_supervisory_orders

predicates.supervisory_review_proceeding: The proceeding asks the High Court to supervise whether a subordinate court or tribunal acted within its authority and according to law.
predicates.single_judge_disposition: A single judge of the High Court disposes of the proceeding.
predicates.order_exercises_supervisory_power: The single judge’s order is made in the exercise of supervisory power over a subordinate court or tribunal.
predicates.charter_excludes_supervisory_orders: The High Court’s charter excludes orders made in the exercise of supervisory power from its intra-court appeal provision.

issues.definition: An intra-court appeal is not maintainable when a single judge disposes of a supervisory-review proceeding by exercising supervisory power and the charter excludes such orders from appeal.

issues.legal_issue: A procedural rule assigning certain writ proceedings to a single judge and providing for their final disposal does not, by itself, remove an appeal right granted by the High Court’s charter.
material_facts: The High Court’s rules ordinarily assigned certain applications under Articles 226 and 227 to a division bench.
A rule allowed specified applications to be heard and finally disposed of by a single judge notwithstanding those ordinary assignments.
The appellants relied on the rule’s words concerning final disposal to argue that no further appeal was available.
issues.conclusion: The words providing for final disposal by a single judge do not themselves bar an intra-court appeal granted by the charter; any applicable bar must arise from the charter or another enactment.
issues.legal_principle: The rule’s non obstante clause permits a single judge to hear and dispose of specified applications, rather than merely issue an initial rule, despite the ordinary assignment of those applications to a division bench. It does not override the charter-based right of appeal. The court relied on Article 225 and the Bombay High Court Appellate Side Rules, particularly Rule 18 of Chapter XVII.

rule.if: specified_constitutional_proceeding and single_judge_final_disposal and procedural_rule_assigns_single_judge and charter_allows_intra_court_appeal and appeal_not_otherwise_barred

predicates.specified_constitutional_proceeding: The proceeding is one of the constitutional applications that the High Court’s procedural rules permit a single judge to decide.
predicates.single_judge_final_disposal: A single judge hears and finally disposes of the proceeding.
predicates.procedural_rule_assigns_single_judge: A High Court procedural rule assigns the proceeding to a single judge despite the ordinary assignment to a division bench.
predicates.charter_allows_intra_court_appeal: The High Court’s charter provides an intra-court appeal from the single judge’s judgment.
predicates.appeal_not_otherwise_barred: No applicable exclusion or other enactment bars the appeal.

issues.definition: A rule permitting a single judge to finally dispose of a proceeding does not defeat a charter-based appeal right when no other bar applies.

issues.legal_issue: When the facts justify seeking relief under either writ or supervisory jurisdiction and an applicant invokes both, the application should be treated as one under writ jurisdiction if that preserves an available appeal right and the substantial order is made in that jurisdiction.
material_facts: The court considered applications framed under both Articles 226 and 227.

It held that where the facts justified an application under either article, treating the application as one under Article 226 could preserve an appeal right when the substantial part of the order was under Article 226, even if the final order also contained ancillary directions pertaining to Article 227.
issues.conclusion: In those circumstances, the application should be treated as made under Article 226, and ancillary directions pertaining to Article 227 should not deprive the applicant of an available appeal under the charter.
issues.legal_principle: The powers under Articles 226 and 227 are distinct and operate in different fields: Article 226 permits directions, orders, and writs to persons, authorities, or government, while Article 227 provides supervisory control over subordinate courts and tribunals. Where an application invokes both and the facts support either, fairness requires treating it as an Article 226 application when the substantial part of the order is under that article, so as not to deprive the applicant of a valuable appeal right. The court agreed with Aidal Singh v. Karan Singh, Raj Kishan Jain v. Tulsi Dass, and Barham Dutt v. Peoples’ Co-operative Transport Society Ltd.

rule.if: combined_writ_and_supervisory_application and facts_support_either_basis and substantial_order_under_writ_jurisdiction and charter_allows_intra_court_appeal and appeal_not_otherwise_barred

predicates.combined_writ_and_supervisory_applicatio: The applicant invokes both writ jurisdiction and supervisory jurisdiction in the same application.
predicates.facts_support_either_basis: The facts would justify seeking relief under either form of jurisdiction.
predicates.substantial_order_under_writ_jurisdictio: The substantial part of the order sought to be appealed is made in the exercise of writ jurisdiction.
predicates.charter_allows_intra_court_appeal: The High Court’s charter provides an intra-court appeal from the relevant single judge’s judgment.
predicates.appeal_not_otherwise_barred: No applicable exclusion or other enactment bars the appeal.

issues.definition: When a combined application is supportable on either basis and its substantial order is under writ jurisdiction, it is treated as a writ proceeding for appeal if an appeal is available and not otherwise barred.
